patient.name: Denis Okonkwo
patient.chief_complaint: Progressive distal leg weakness and sensory loss over 6 months with POEMS features
patient.hpi: Denis Okonkwo is a 47-year-old civil engineer presenting with a 6-month history of progressive bilateral leg weakness and sensory loss. His symptoms began with bilateral foot tingling and numbness, followed by progressive weakness over the subsequent 2 months, and he now has significant difficulty walking distances more than half a block without stopping. He notes that his symptoms began with what seemed like a typical neuropathy but he has developed several additional features that concern him: prominent bilateral ankle and calf swelling, a change in his skin color with darkening of his face and forearms, and coarsening of his body hair. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer in remission 6 years ago and is cancer-anxiety prone. He was initially evaluated by an oncologist who ordered imaging to exclude cancer recurrence — CT was negative. He saw a dermatologist for the skin changes who documented 'hyperpigmentation, uncertain etiology.' He also reports that his libido has significantly decreased over the past 6 months and he was found to have low testosterone on a routine check (188 ng/dL). He has had no fever, no night sweats, no lymph node swelling. He is a non-smoker and social drinker (2-3 drinks per week). His primary care physician has been perplexed by the combination of symptoms and referred him to neurology.
pmh: Prostate cancer (low-grade, localized — in remission 6 years, no active treatment)

report.summary: SEVERELY ABNORMAL NCS/EMG. DEMYELINATING SENSORIMOTOR POLYNEUROPATHY with superimposed axonal loss — POEMS syndrome neuropathy pattern. Consistent with VEGF-mediated nerve vasculature disruption causing both demyelination and axonal injury.

motor.flag: markedly prolonged DML, low amplitude, slow velocity — mixed demyelinating + axonal
prolonged DML, reduced amplitude, slow velocity

emg.summary: Mixed demyelinating and axonal pattern. Consistent with POEMS syndrome neuropathy.

report.overall_impression: Severe demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy with superimposed axonal loss. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies, severely slowed conduction velocities, and reduced CMAP amplitudes across all tested motor nerves. Sural and median SNAP amplitudes severely reduced with slowed velocities. Needle EMG shows active and chronic denervation in distal musculature. Findings are consistent with a severe mixed demyelinating and axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

specialized_test.impression: 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies (peroneal 8.2 ms, tibial 8.8 ms, median 6.4 ms) with severely slowed conduction velocities (peroneal 31.4 m/s, tibial 32.8 m/s) and reduced CMAP amplitudes across all tested motor nerves. 2. Sural and median SNAP amplitudes severely reduced with slowed sensory velocities. 3. Needle EMG: active denervation (fibrillations) and chronic neuropathic motor units in distal upper and lower extremity musculature. Findings are consistent with a severe mixed demyelinating and axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with symmetric four-limb involvement. Clinical correlation recommended.

report.summary: FDG-PET/CT: TWO osteosclerotic lesions identified: (1) L2 vertebra — osteosclerotic lesion (SUV 2.8, sclerotic morphology on CT), (2) Left iliac bone — osteosclerotic lesion (SUV 3.1). No lytic lesions. No lymphoma pattern. No Castleman disease adenopathy. Prostate: no FDG uptake at prostatectomy bed — confirmed complete prostate cancer remission (not the cause of POEMS).
report.clinical_significance: Two osteosclerotic lesions identified: L2 vertebra (SUV 2.8, sclerotic morphology on CT) and left iliac bone (SUV 3.1). No FDG-avid lytic lesions. No lymphomatous adenopathy pattern. No FDG uptake at prostatectomy bed. Clinical correlation recommended.

report.summary: Bone marrow biopsy (iliac crest): IgA lambda plasma cells 6% — borderline (POEMS with osteosclerotic myeloma often has low BM PC%). No Castleman disease features. Lambda-restricted plasma cell clusters in peritrabecular pattern. Osteosclerotic changes at biopsy site. Consistent with osteosclerotic myeloma underlying POEMS.
report.interpretation: IgA lambda-restricted plasma cells comprising 6% of cellularity. Peritrabecular plasma cell clusters with lambda light chain restriction on immunohistochemistry. Osteosclerotic changes identified at the biopsy site. No features of Castleman disease. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: IgA lambda-restricted plasma cells comprising 6% of total marrow cellularity, arranged in peritrabecular clusters with lambda light chain restriction confirmed on immunohistochemistry. Osteosclerotic stromal changes identified at the biopsy site. No morphological features of Castleman disease. No high-grade plasma cell proliferation. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: TSH 3.2 mIU/L (within normal limits). Testosterone 324 ng/dL (within normal limits). HbA1c 6.8% (H). Clinical correlation recommended.

report.summary: Fundoscopy: bilateral papilledema grade 1 confirmed. OCT: bilateral RNFL thickening (right 182 mcm, left 168 mcm; reference <120 mcm). Visual acuity 20/20 bilaterally. Visual fields: bilateral blind spot enlargement only. No visual loss currently. POEMS-mediated intracranial hypertension — VEGF increases CNS vascular permeability and ICP.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: POEMS syndrome from multifocal osteosclerotic myeloma (IgA lambda) — straightforward presentation with classical features
critical_actions: Order VEGF level — markedly elevated VEGF is pathognomonic for POEMS and drives all organ manifestations
Perform fundoscopy in EVERY neuropathy evaluation — papilledema would be missed without it
Comprehensive endocrine panel — POEMS causes multiple simultaneous endocrine deficiencies
Provide adrenal insufficiency stress dosing protocol — risk of adrenal crisis if patient becomes ill or has surgery without doubled hydrocortisone dose
FDG-PET/CT — identifies multifocal vs solitary osteosclerotic disease, determining if radiation alone is possible
contraindicated_actions: Do not treat with IVIG — POEMS is IVIG-refractory
Do not attribute endocrine abnormalities to independent coincidental findings — all are VEGF-mediated manifestations of POEMS
Do not attribute neuropathy to prostate cancer without excluding POEMS when M-protein is present
Do not miss stress dosing instruction for adrenal insufficiency — patient must double hydrocortisone dose during illness or surgery

differential.key_features: CIDP does not cause papilledema, edema, endocrinopathy, skin changes, or markedly elevated VEGF; M-protein 1.4 g/dL and thrombocytosis are not CIDP features

differential.diagnosis: Prostate cancer recurrence with paraneoplastic neuropathy
differential.key_features: PSA undetectable, PET-CT negative at prostatectomy bed; osteosclerotic lesions are plasma cell lesions (IgA lambda), not prostate metastases
MEN involves pituitary + parathyroid + pancreas/thyroid; endocrine failure here is VEGF-mediated (all three affected simultaneously), not MEN; no hypercalcemia, no insulinoma features

key_reasoning_points: STRAIGHTFORWARD REAL-SEEDED: Classic POEMS presentation with all major features visible — the real-seeded element is the prostate cancer history creating initial anchoring toward malignant neuropathy

POEMS DIAGNOSIS FRAMEWORK: Mandatory criteria (polyneuropathy + monoclonal protein) plus major criteria (VEGF elevation, papilledema, osteosclerotic lesions) make this a straightforward POEMS diagnosis once the workup is systematically pursued

VEGF IS KEY: Measuring VEGF converts a confusing multi-system presentation into a single pathogenic explanation — all manifestations (neuropathy, edema, papilledema, endocrinopathy, skin changes) are VEGF-mediated
PROSTATE CANCER RED HERRING: Prior cancer history in neuropathy patients always requires exclusion; PSA undetectable and PET-CT negative at prostatectomy bed definitively exclude recurrence
MULTIFOCAL OSTEOSCLEROTIC MYELOMA: Two lesions require systemic treatment (lenalidomide + dexamethasone → ASCT) rather than radiation alone (which is for solitary plasmacytoma)
